rule: All interactive elements must have minimum 44x44px touch target with 8px spacing
rationale: WCAG 2.5.5 — prevents mis-taps on mobile, critical for motor impairments

rule: Color contrast ratio minimum 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text
rationale: WCAG 1.4.3 — text must be readable for low-vision users

rule: All images must have descriptive alt text or empty alt for decorative images
rationale: WCAG 1.1.1 — screen readers depend on alt text for context

rule: Focus indicator must be visible: 3-4px outline with sufficient contrast
rationale: WCAG 2.4.7 — keyboard users must see where focus is

rule: Skip navigation link as first focusable element on every page
rationale: WCAG 2.4.1 — keyboard users should skip repetitive nav

rule: Respect prefers-reduced-motion media query — disable animations when set
rationale: WCAG 2.3.3 — motion can cause vestibular disorders

rule: Form inputs must have visible labels (not just placeholder text)
rationale: WCAG 1.3.1 — placeholders disappear on focus, breaking context

rule: Error messages must identify the field and describe what went wrong
rationale: WCAG 3.3.1 — users need to know what to fix and where

rule: Implement smooth scrolling with offset for fixed headers
rationale: Prevents content hiding under sticky nav, improves perceived polish

rule: Sticky navigation must not exceed 64px height on desktop or 48px on mobile
rationale: Excessive nav steals viewport space, especially on small screens

rule: Breadcrumbs for any page deeper than 2 levels in hierarchy
rationale: Users need orientation in deep navigation structures

rule: Deep links must scroll to and highlight the target section
rationale: Shared URLs should land users at the exact content referenced

rule: Mobile hamburger menu must be reachable with one thumb (bottom-right preferred)
rationale: Thumb zone accessibility — top-left is hardest to reach on large phones

rule: Images must use next-gen formats (WebP/AVIF) with fallback
rationale: Reduces page weight 25-50% vs PNG/JPEG without quality loss

rule: Implement skeleton screens instead of spinners for loading states
rationale: Perceived performance improves — users see structure before content

rule: Lazy load images and heavy components below the fold
rationale: First Contentful Paint improves when above-fold loads first

rule: Use CSS content-visibility: auto for long scrollable lists
rationale: Browser skips rendering off-screen items, massive perf gain

rule: Font loading: use font-display: swap with preloaded critical fonts
rationale: Prevents invisible text flash (FOIT), shows fallback instantly

rule: Limit hero animations to 1-2 key elements — never animate everything
rationale: Too many animations create cognitive overload and feel cheap

rule: Micro-interactions should be 150-300ms — never exceed 500ms
rationale: Longer animations feel sluggish; shorter ones feel instant and responsive

rule: Use ease-out for entering elements and ease-in for exiting elements
rationale: Matches natural physics — objects decelerate arriving, accelerate leaving

rule: Stagger list item animations by 50-80ms per item, max 5 items
rationale: Creates rhythm without making users wait; cap prevents long sequences

rule: Loading indicators must appear after 300ms delay — not instantly
rationale: Instant spinners for fast operations create unnecessary visual noise

rule: Maintain consistent 8px spacing grid throughout the application
rationale: Visual rhythm and alignment; easier to maintain proportional spacing

rule: Maximum text line width: 65-75 characters for optimal readability
rationale: Beyond 75 chars, eye tracking becomes difficult and reading speed drops

rule: Use dvh (dynamic viewport height) instead of vh on mobile
rationale: 100vh on mobile includes address bar space, causing overflow

rule: Z-index scale: base(0) overlays(100) modals(200) toasts(300) tooltips(400)
rationale: Prevents z-index wars and unpredictable stacking

rule: Reserve space for dynamic content to prevent layout shift (CLS)
rationale: Cumulative Layout Shift hurts UX and Core Web Vitals score

rule: Double-submit prevention on all form buttons (disable after first click)
rationale: Prevents duplicate transactions — critical for payment and data mutations

rule: Provide immediate visual feedback on every user action within 100ms
rationale: Users need confirmation their action registered — even before completion

rule: Destructive actions require confirmation dialog with explicit action text
rationale: Delete button should say 'Delete project' not just 'OK' — prevents accidents

rule: Empty states must include clear call-to-action, not just 'No data'
rationale: Empty screens are onboarding opportunities — guide users to next action

rule: Toast notifications auto-dismiss in 3-5 seconds, errors persist until dismissed
rationale: Success is transient, errors need user attention and action

rule: Use system font stack as fallback: -apple-system BlinkMacSystemFont Segoe UI
rationale: Ensures readable text even before custom fonts load

rule: Heading hierarchy must be sequential: h1 > h2 > h3 (never skip levels)
rationale: Screen readers use heading levels for navigation structure

rule: Body text minimum 16px on mobile, 14px on desktop with 1.5 line-height
rationale: Below these sizes, readability drops significantly especially on mobile

rule: Limit to 2-3 font families maximum per project
rationale: Too many fonts create visual chaos and increase load time

rule: Mobile-first approach: design for 375px then scale up
rationale: Forces content prioritization — mobile constraints reveal what matters

rule: Breakpoints: 640px (sm) 768px (md) 1024px (lg) 1280px (xl) 1536px (2xl)
rationale: Matches Tailwind defaults and covers all common device sizes

rule: Test at 320px width minimum — some devices still use this
rationale: iPhone SE and budget Android devices have narrow viewports

rule: Tables must be horizontally scrollable or card-transformed on mobile
rationale: Tables wider than viewport are unusable without scroll

rule: Semantic colors: success(green) warning(amber) error(red) info(blue)
rationale: Consistent color meaning across the app reduces cognitive load

rule: Never use color alone to convey information — add icon or text label
rationale: Color-blind users (8% of males) cannot distinguish color-only signals

rule: Dark mode: reduce white to #E2E8F0 and use dark gray #0F172A not pure black
rationale: Pure white on pure black causes eye strain; slight reduction is gentler

rule: Limit accent color usage to 10-15% of the UI surface area
rationale: Accent overuse dilutes its attention-drawing purpose
